title: Why Do Money Fund Managers Voluntarily Waive Their Fees?
authors: Susan E. K. Christoffersen
full_text_accessible: YES (June 2000 manuscript; journal version not opened)
research_question: Why do money-fund managers voluntarily waive contractual fees?
data_and_sample: Lipper annual MMF data 1990-1995 plus IBC Donoghue quarterly waivers 1993-1994
identification: Panel/cross-sectional associations of waivers with performance and expected flows; retail vs institutional comparison
main_results: Over half of MMF managers waive; retail managers adjust net fees to realized performance and expected flows (waivers act as a flexible, quasi performance-based fee). Section on 'option value of waiving' says recapturing higher fees later is a possible motive and that 'more research on the option value of waiving is necessary'.
connection_to_our_question: Owns the economics of voluntary waivers as flexible pricing; explicitly leaves the recapture/option-value motive open. Closest conceptual ancestor for E-R1/E-R2.
overlap: Direct (conceptual), indirect (empirical setting: MMFs 1990s, voluntary not contractual-recoupable waivers)
notes: Christoffersen's 1998 Penn dissertation 'Fee waivers in mutual funds' (ProQuest 9913445) and Wharton FIC WP 97-46 belong to the same research program; not counted as separate contributions.

title: The Puzzle of ESG Fund Fees
authors: Aaron J. Black; Julian F. Koelbel
research_question: Why do U.S. ESG funds charge lower net fees?
data_and_sample: CRSP survivor-bias-free MF data Q1 2011-Q2 2024 (~14,000 series) plus SEC Mutual Fund Prospectus Risk/Return data for gross fees and waivers (355,873 non-ESG and 8,000 ESG fund-quarter waiver obs.)
identification: Panel regressions with year x CRSP-style FE and within-provider comparisons
main_results: ESG funds' net expense ratios 9.5-12.7 bp lower, driven by larger/more frequent waivers; cross-selling explanation favoured; funds that discontinue waivers show no higher subsequent fee changes at t+4/t+8 (no 'raise fees later' evidence)
connection_to_our_question: Most recent paper that treats waivers as strategic pricing and tests a 'waive now, raise later' story with SEC prospectus data; does not use recoupment rights, N-CEN or recovery amounts
overlap: Indirect-to-direct (closest recent empirical competitor on waiver strategy)
notes: Confirms SEC prospectus Risk/Return data carry class-level waiver amounts and fee-table footnotes usable at scale.
